query: Consider the following context: Temper embrittlement, characterized by a dramatic loss of ductility within a narrow temperature window, is ubiquitous in conventional alloys but is not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems. In that context, which material can be used for ductile–brittle–ductile transition, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Conventional alloys can exhibit a ductile–brittle–ductile transition when subjected to systematic temperature variation, which can be understood by combining experimental and simulation techniques.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional alloys with a known temper embrittlement history
generation.conditions: Narrow temperature window where temper embrittlement occurs
generation.mechanism: Thermally-activated diffusion and segregation of impurities at grain boundaries
generation.predicted_outcome: A dramatic loss of ductility within the narrow temperature window, followed by a recovery of ductility at higher temperatures
generation.baseline: Room temperature ductility of the conventional alloy
generation.boundary: Temperature range where temper embrittlement is observed
generation.uncertainty: The exact temperature range and magnitude of the ductile–brittle–ductile transition may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing history

falsification_experiment.design: Combine systematic temperature variation experiments with molecular dynamics simulations to study the ductile–brittle–ductile transition in conventional alloys
measurements: Simulation-based analysis of grain boundary segregation and precipitation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimental and simulation results do not show a correlation between the ductile–brittle–ductile transition and the thermally-activated diffusion and segregation of impurities at grain boundaries, the hypothesis is falsified.

frame.system: conventional alloys vs compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems
frame.limitation: temper embrittlement and loss of ductility in conventional alloys
constraints: compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems

families.principle: Integration of experimental and simulation techniques to understand the ductile–brittle–ductile transition
families.best_lever: Combining systematic temperature variation experiments with molecular dynamics simulations

families.principle: Systematic variation of temperature and composition to identify the ductile–brittle–ductile transition
cues_against: not reported in compositionally complex or high‐entropy alloy systems
families.best_lever: Systematic temperature variation in conventional alloys

families.principle: Real-time observation of microstructural changes during the ductile–brittle–ductile transition
cues_against: not directly related to material selection
families.best_lever: In-situ TEM or SEM characterization of conventional alloys

families.principle: Simulation of atomic-scale mechanisms governing the ductile–brittle–ductile transition
cues_against: may not directly address the material selection
families.best_lever: Molecular dynamics simulation of conventional alloys

frame.limitation: temper embrittlement and loss of ductility in conventional alloys
